name: Speed skating
energy: From mostly anaerobic in the 500 m to mostly aerobic over 5,000 to 10,000 m, all in a deep crouch that restricts blood flow to the thighs.
summary: Speed skating is repeated sideways leg pushes from a deep crouch, and back pain, knee overuse and falls are the main problems. The plan builds deep-knee leg strength and lateral power, adductor and hip strength, a robust lower and upper back, and an aerobic base mainly on the bike.

evidence.claim: Seasonal back pain prevalence reaches up to 84% in long and short track skaters, and no study has yet tested whether any prevention measure works.
evidence.source: Hendricks, Verhagen & van de Water 2024, Scand J Med Sci Sports

evidence.claim: In elite youth long track skaters the knee had the highest repetitive injury burden (11 days lost per 1,000 h), followed by the thoracic spine.
evidence.source: Hendricks, van de Water & Verhagen 2024, Br J Sports Med

evidence.claim: Reference levels for 30 s anaerobic power in national team skaters: senior men average 12.4-13.3 W/kg peak power, very high above 14.25.

variants.name: Long track
variants.desc: 400 m oval, 500 m to 10,000 m; sprinters need max strength and power, distance skaters need aerobic capacity and crouch endurance.
variants.note: Sprinters keep heavy strength and jumps; distance skaters swap some power work for bike volume.

variants.name: Short track
variants.desc: 111 m oval, 500 m to 1500 m pack racing with tight left turns, crossovers, surges, contact and falls.
variants.note: More lateral power and single-leg work, neck strength for falls, and longer recovery after ice sessions.

variants.name: Inline speed skating
variants.desc: Same crouched stride on wheels, on track and road, with long road races and crashes on hard ground.
variants.note: More aerobic work for road races and wrist protection for falls; the outdoor season runs spring to autumn.

off.name: Max strength in the crouch
off.focus: Deep-knee leg strength and vertical power.

slots.note: Work to below a 100 deg knee angle, the skating position.

off.name: Lateral power and hips
off.focus: Side-to-side push power, single-leg strength and the lower back.

slots.note: Land in the skating position and hold 1 s.

off.name: Upper back, trunk and crouch endurance
off.focus: Thoracic strength and the ability to hold the skating position.

slots.note: Hold the skating knee angle; also loads the patellar tendon.

in.name: Race season strength
in.focus: Hold strength and power in 30-35 minutes.

in.name: Back and trunk top-up
in.focus: Short session to keep the back robust through the season.

off.name: Aerobic bike base
off.intensity: Easy to moderate, can hold a conversation
off.why: Cycling is the usual skater cross-training and uses a similar crouched leg action (practice).

off.name: Aerobic intervals
off.why: Raises aerobic power for 1500 m and longer races.

pre.name: Race-pace intervals
pre.why: Lactate tolerance for 500-1500 m efforts; 800 m time trials produced lactate of about 10-11 mmol/L (Hettinga 2016).

pre.name: Dryland skating imitation
pre.work: 6-10 x 30 s skating-position side jumps or slide board

in.name: Easy aerobic ride
in.why: Keeps the aerobic base without adding fatigue in race weeks.

tests.name: 30 s all-out bike sprint
tests.how: Wattbike or Monark at 7.5% of body mass, 30 s all-out from a rolling start; record peak power per kg.
tests.note: Senior men from Polish national team data (Sitkowski 2025). Senior women: average 10.66-11.41, very high above 12.16.

tests.name: Standing broad jump
tests.how: Two-foot take-off, stick the landing, measure to the back heel; best of 3.
tests.note: Practice bands for men; women about 15-20% lower.

tests.name: Single-leg lateral bound
tests.how: From one leg, bound sideways and stick on the other leg; measure inside foot to inside foot, best of 3 each way.
tests.note: No verified norms; height dependent. Flag a left-right gap above 10-15% (practice).

tests.name: Countermovement jump
tests.how: Hands on hips, jump mat or My Jump app, best of 3.
tests.note: Practice bands for men; women about 20% lower.

tests.name: Estimated squat 1RM
tests.how: Work up to a 3-5RM back or front squat and estimate 1RM; divide by body mass.
tests.note: Practice bands for men; women about 0.2-0.3 lower. Not for under-16s.

week: Race weekend: heavy lower session Monday or Tuesday.
Lateral power and back work Wednesday at the latest.
Short track sessions need more recovery; avoid heavy lifting the day after a hard ice session.
No heavy lower work within 72 h of racing.
Day after racing: easy ride and mobility.
primer: Dynamic warm-up and easy bike or jog
Then the normal on-ice warm-up with starts

lines: Last heavy lower lift 5-7 days before the race.
Gym volume down about 50%, keep the load.
Keep a few short race-pace efforts, cut total volume.
Short track: allow an extra recovery day after the hardest ice session.

rules: Back pain is the most common complaint: do the back work every week, all year.
Short track: helmet, cut-resistant suit, neck guard, shin and ankle protection in every session.
Inline: helmet and wrist guards on the road.
Plan off-ice load as carefully as ice; many short track injuries happen off ice.
Under 16: no 1RM testing and no depth jumps.
